title: agent-memory atom (L1) — v1
description: One atomic memory claim extracted from an L0 transcript. Every atom MUST carry a live back-pointer into the transcript that produced it; an atom without provenance is discarded, never stored. Promotion to L2/L3 is decided by recurrence across distinct sessions, not by importance. See ../DESIGN.md sections 3 and 4.

id.description: Stable id, PROJECT-SCOPED: hash(normalized_claim + '\u0000' + project) when scope is 'project', hash(normalized_claim) when scope is 'global'. The project component is mandatory and is what stops two unrelated claims that normalize alike in different repos (e.g. 'tests must pass before merge') from colliding and merging their 'sessions' arrays across projects — which would manufacture false durability, since the L1 to L2 gate requires the sessions be from the SAME project. Merging on this id is how a claim re-observed in a later session accumulates durability instead of duplicating.

claim.description: A single assertion, stated positively and in the present tense. One claim per atom — a sentence containing 'and' is usually two atoms.

scope.description: 'project' claims are candidates for L2, 'global' for L3. Scope is assigned at extraction and may be widened by promotion, never narrowed automatically.

project.description: Repo or working-directory slug. REQUIRED when scope is 'project'; MUST be absent when scope is 'global'.

kind.description: constraint = a rule that must hold (PR base is dev). preference = a stated liking (stdlib only). fact = an environmental truth (backend URL). decision = a choice made with rationale. failure = a command or approach that did not work, retained so it is not retried.

first_seen.description: UTC timestamp of the earliest observation. Never updated after creation.

last_seen.description: UTC timestamp of the most recent observation. Drives the 90-day L1 expiry and recency scoring at recall.

observations.description: Total times observed. Informational — the promotion gate counts distinct entries in 'sessions', NOT this field, so restating a claim repeatedly within one session cannot manufacture durability.

sessions.description: Set of distinct Claude Code session ids in which this claim was observed. This is the durability counter that gates promotion (L1 to L2 needs >= 3 distinct sessions across >= 2 distinct days).

source.description: Back-pointer into L0 for the MOST RECENT observation: '<transcript path>#L<line>'. Overwritten on every merge — read 'first_source' for the evidence that originally justified the claim. Required for promotion; an unprovenanced claim can never be promoted. This is the anti-fabrication rule.

first_source.description: Back-pointer into L0 for the FIRST observation, written once at creation and never overwritten. 'source' alone is insufficient for an anti-fabrication field: after N merges it points only at the latest sighting, so the evidence that originally justified the claim would be unrecoverable exactly when an auditor needs it. Both are retained deliberately.

promoted_from_projects.description: Projects in which this claim independently held at L2 before being promoted to L3. REQUIRED once tier is L3. Exists because 'scope' flips to 'global' on promotion and the conditional below then forbids the single 'project' field — without this array the >= 2-distinct-projects criterion from DESIGN.md section 4.1 would be unauditable the moment it was satisfied, discarding the evidence precisely when it turns from an eligibility test into an audit trail.

confidence.description: observed = the agent inferred it (3 sessions to promote). stated = the user said it directly (2 sessions). verified = a script or check confirmed it (promotes on 1 observation; it is not hearsay).

tier.description: Current tier. L0 is never represented as an atom — it is the raw transcript this atom points back to.

contested.description: Set when a newer atom contradicts this one. A contested L2/L3 claim is STILL injected, tagged with the conflict — silently withholding it would be worse than surfacing it. Resolution is always a human decision at adopt time.

contested_by.description: Ids of atoms contradicting this claim.

promoted_at.description: When this atom last changed tier. Starts the 30-day clock for L2 to L3 eligibility.

redacted.description: True when the redaction pass altered the claim text before storage. A redacted atom is still usable, but is never promoted to a committed tier without human review.

examples.claim: PR base branch is dev, never main
Python tooling stays stdlib-only; no third-party runtime deps
